structuredContent.governing_intent: Create a single reviewable CANDIDATE architecture/design document at docs/architecture/pre-python-gate/domain-model.md, plus only local packet/readiness evidence, for Pre-Python domain modeling. The work is documentation-only, must reuse cited authority, preserve existing Founder-resolved decisions, and must not implement, edit EOS/Node/source/config/tests, or treat the candidate model as approved architecture.
structuredContent.summary: The packet has a coherent bounded outcome: draft the domain-model candidate artifact covering ubiquitous language, identities, invariants, owners, non-examples, lifecycle meanings, bounded contexts, EOS mapping, source/invariant traceability, contract semantics, examples, limitations, and explicit Founder-review decisions. Material owner intent is sufficiently constrained: unresolved architecture/product decisions should be recorded as candidate review items rather than silently resolved. The task is ready for autonomous documentation work and independent content review.
implementation_unknowns: Exact contents and section locations of the cited local baselines must be inspected during implementation and traced accurately; the supplied text reports their existence but this assessment does not verify them.

The author must reconcile terminology across reset sections, EOS ADR/ontology, canonical architecture responsibility lists, Node behavior evidence, and the binding architecture authority without renaming either AlienIntent or EOS vocabularies.
The document structure, traceability table format, example scenario format, and local packet/readiness evidence format are implementation choices to be selected within the provided constraints.

The documentation checker or review mechanism for path/coverage validation must be identified or applied if available in the repository; otherwise the artifact should include enough explicit traceability for manual independent review.
structuredContent.verification_assessment: Acceptance is observable against one meaningful independent verdict: a reviewer can inspect the produced domain-model.md and local evidence to confirm it defines canonical terms, identities, invariants, owners, examples/non-examples, preserves BIU and all ten lifecycle meanings, proposes bounded contexts and relationships, maps EOS terms without vocabulary substitution, labels proposed semantics as CANDIDATE, records unresolved Founder decisions, respects documentation-only exclusions, and traces claims to cited source authority. Verification need not execute runtime tests because the packet explicitly limits work to architecture documentation and states no new runtime regression runs are warranted.
material_risks: The artifact could accidentally promote candidate architecture to approved authority instead of clearly labeling it as CANDIDATE for Founder review.
The author could invent new domain semantics or repository structure instead of reusing and reconciling cited source material.
Cross-document choices may be silently adopted from neighboring documents rather than recorded as unresolved candidate decisions.
EOS source is only a candidate conformance pin, so over-adopting draft EOS material would exceed the stated authority.

The task depends on accurately preserving existing Founder decisions, especially BIU, lifecycle semantics, Node/Python coexistence, no-polling, DDD/Hexagonal/ACL boundaries, and documentation-only scope.
structuredContent.next_action: Proceed to draft the candidate domain-model.md and its local readiness/packet evidence within the authorized documentation paths, using the cited baselines for traceability and explicitly listing any material Founder-review decisions instead of resolving them silently.
structuredContent.rationale: The controlling condition is READY because the packet establishes a clear documentation outcome, bounded paths, governing authority, exclusions, acceptance criteria, verification approach, and treatment of unresolved architecture decisions. Remaining uncertainty is primarily engineering/document-authoring research—locating source material, structuring traceability, and reconciling terminology—not unresolved owner intent. The work is cohesive: the ubiquitous language and bounded-context model are interdependent parts of one reviewable domain-model candidate, and splitting them would risk losing coherence rather than isolating independent decision centers.
